text: Can you describe exactly where the pain is located in your neck and arms, and does it radiate into your fingers? Have you noticed any specific weakness, such as difficulty holding objects or dropping things?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old male. The patient reports a year-long history of burning pain in his neck and arms, accompanying paresthesias in his hands. Over the past 3 months, he has experienced increasing weakness in both hands. He has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypercholesterolemia, and hypertension. He was involved in a motor vehicle accident 3 years ago.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for that detailed history. Given your age, the duration of symptoms, and the progression of weakness alongside burning pain and paresthesias, do you experience any numbness or tingling that travels down the outside of your arms to the thumb, index, or middle fingers? speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Burning pain in neck and arms, and weakness in both hands. I also have Paresthesias in hands, Absent reflexes, Decreased hand grip with fasciculations. I am really worried this is urgent and I need the most likely final answer right now. Please do not delay by exploring too many alternative possibilities.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Based on your history of diabetes, the specific distribution of your symptoms (burning pain, paresthesias, and weakness), and the physical exam findings of absent reflexes, fasciculations, and decreased grip strength, I have reached a conclusion.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Cervical Spondylotic Myelopathy with Superimposed Polyneuropathy
